blocks.text: Setting up Gmail for your Mac workflow

Google does not offer a native desktop app for macOS. Many publicists use Safari or Chrome to build a dedicated web app. Open Gmail in Safari and go to File > Add to Dock. This creates an icon in your dock that behaves like a standalone app. It keeps your email separate from your general browsing tabs. This is helpful when you have multiple research windows open for media monitoring.
Using keyboard shortcuts to save time

Shortcuts are essential for managing the high volume of emails you receive. They are disabled by default. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts to turn them on. Once enabled, press ? to see a cheat sheet of all available commands. Memorize c for compose and e for archive. These two alone will change how you clear your inbox.

Publicists often struggle with keeping media contacts organized. Use Gmail labels to categorize emails by book title or media outlet type. Create a filter to automatically move incoming emails from known journalists into a specific label. This keeps your primary inbox clean for urgent author requests. If you need to find an attachment quickly, use the search operators like has:attachment to narrow down your results.

blocks.text: One common mistake is leaving too many emails in the inbox. This leads to missed deadlines and increased stress. Try to process emails in batches rather than checking them every five minutes. Each time you switch from a task to check your inbox, you lose focus. It takes 23 minutes to get back into a deep work state. Stick to checking your email at set times during the day.
Drafting better pitches on your Mac

Writing press releases and pitches requires focus. Many publicists use Ulysses or Pages to draft their content before moving it to Gmail. This helps with proofreading and keeps your formatting clean. When you are ready to send, copy the text into your Gmail draft. If you need to insert a link or attach a press kit, use the standard Gmail tools. Remember to check your daily sending limits if you are sending a large volume of pitches.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native desktop app for macOS. You should use a browser to create a web app or use a third-party client that supports OAuth.

faq.question: How do I speed up my Gmail workflow?
faq.answer: Enable keyboard shortcuts in your Gmail settings. Using keys like e to archive and c to compose will save significant time throughout your workweek.

faq.question: Can I manage large mailing lists in Gmail?
faq.answer: Gmail has daily sending limits. Personal accounts can send to 500 recipients per day, while Workspace accounts can reach up to 2,000. For larger lists, consider using a dedicated email marketing tool.

faq.question: How do I avoid email distractions?
faq.answer: Process your inbox in batches rather than keeping a tab open all day. This helps you maintain focus on drafting pitches and media monitoring.
